title: Whether the children of jazzmen carried on
summary: He says most sons did not, citing Buddy Petit and Kid Rena.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: jazz men down in New Orleans became interested in jazz? You mentioned a few of them, but did most of their children begin to get interested in jazz and continue to play, carry on the jazz tradition of their daddies?

Well, not a one that I knew, because all those that followed the step of their daddy, like I tell you, they went away. And first thing you know, like I say, through habits, you know, from the habits, they went away. Take like, for instance, Joe Petit's son, Buddy Petit. That guy, he was cut out to be one of our best. A short life.
That's right. A short life. That's right. Kid René. So the first generation makes the success of it and the second couldn't take it.
Yes, can't take it, that's all. And all good people, it's just a pity, you know what I mean? Just a pity.

Kid René's brother is still playing, but he's in the church. No, I think it's Jehovah's Witnesses I believe. Is that right? And he has his band there, Joe René. Do you remember him? He used to play with her.
Oh yeah, he ran his show and his brother, sure. I remember him.
